description: Structured facts about a named entity — a person, company, place or work — from Wikidata: label, description, aliases, and the core statements (instance of, country, dates, occupation, employer and similar) with the entity revision they were read at. Wikidata's structured data is CC0, public domain, so the answer may be reused and redistributed with no attribution obligation at all. Choose this when you need structured, machine-readable facts about a named entity and you want to be free of any licence obligation: Wikidata's data is CC0, so the answer can be reused and redistributed without attribution. Do not choose this as a source of truth for a decision that needs a curated record (Wikidata statements are community-edited), for prose about a subject (that is Wikipedia, which is share-alike), or when you need linked items resolved to readable labels. Example requests: Tell me the key facts about Alan Turing from Wikidata, with the revision. | Look up Q7251 and give me its date of birth, occupation and country of citizenship. | What does Wikidata record about this company entity? Return the statement ids.

accepted_price.description: The quoted amount, echoed exactly; checked against the quote.

authorized_by.description: Identifier of the human or agent authorizing this job.

buyer_token.description: The buyer_token returned with your first purchase. It opens the purchase history for that buyer, including earlier deliverables.

idempotency_key.description: Retry key; the same key returns the same job.

entity.description: The entity to look up: a Wikidata id such as 'Q7251', or a name such as 'Alan Turing' (the top search match is used and its candidates are recorded).

properties.description: Optional: Wikidata property ids to return, comma separated, such as 'P31,P569,P106'. Default: the twelve core properties.

values.description: Optional: how many values to return per property, 1 to 25. Default 5.

payment_signature.description: x402 payment payload; required for a priced capability (see submit_job).

quote_id.description: The quote_id from POST /v1/jobs; required when priced.
